title: Quarterly roadmap: Dedicated capacity autoscaling and burst policy planning
creator: Marisol Vega
description: Quarterly planning ticket to define the roadmap and success criteria for Dedicated Capacity autoscaling (automatic scale-up/scale-down and burst capacity policies). This doc consolidates outcomes from discovery, proposed milestones, cross-functional dependencies, and initial acceptance criteria for the Q2 rollout. Goal is to reduce customer over-provisioning while protecting latency SLOs and preserving predictability for committed customers.
objectives: Define a phased roadmap to deliver robust autoscaling for Dedicated GPU pools (predictable scale-down, fast scale-up, and controlled burst capability)
Create a rollout plan that preserves SLA guarantees for reserved capacity and provides clear fallback behavior
Provide UI/API controls for policy definition, cost-estimation, and observability so customers can safely adopt autoscaling
Establish measurable success metrics for customer cost reduction and utilization improvements
milestones: Discovery complete: customer interviews, telemetry analysis, and competitive benchmarks (target: 2026-02-28)
PRD sign-off and API schema for autoscale policies (target: 2026-03-15)
Runtime & scheduler prototype to handle rapid scale-up and KV cache warmup strategies (target: 2026-03-31)
Console UX mocks and policy editor implementation (target: 2026-04-10)
Billing/metric plumbing and cost-estimation model integration (target: 2026-04-15)
Canary rollout with 3 pilot customers and robust rollback policy (target: 2026-04-24)
GA release to Dedicated customers with opt-in pilot and runbook (target: 2026-04-30)
success_metrics: 10-20% reduction in average committed spend for pilot customers after 8 weeks
20% increase in average GPU utilization across autoscaled pools
No degradation of P99 latency by more than 5% compared to baseline
>90% accuracy in cost-estimation UI predictions within 10% of actual spend
Fewer than 2 customer-impacting incidents related to autoscale in first 30 days after GA
acceptance_criteria: API: Autoscale policy CRUD endpoints with validation and stable schema
Runtime: Safe scale-up path with warmup/KV cache priming and fallbacks to pinned capacity
Console: Policy editor, estimated cost preview, and per-pool utilization visualizations
Observability: Dashboards for scaling events, per-policy SLO impact, and cost telemetry
Billing: Accurate per-customer cost attribution for burst usage and autoscaled secs
E2E: Canary passes with 3 pilot customers and documented rollback procedure
Docs: Public docs, quickstart, and runbook for support/SEs
stakeholders: Engineering: Priya Sinha (runtime lead), Daniel Ho (scheduler), Zoe Martinez (billing)
risks: Cold-start latency after scale-up could violate customer latency SLOs without careful warmup
Billing complexity for mixed committed and burst usage may introduce disputes
Autoscaler oscillation under bursty workloads if thresholds not tuned
Cross-tenant isolation concerns when sharing burst nodes across pools
Dependence on low-level runtime kernel scheduling and possible hardware variance across regions
